steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on a paper towel-lined plate. Crumble cooled bacon into a bowl and set aside.

Stir together cream cheese and ranch dressing mix in a bowl until smooth. Spread mixture on the bottom of a pie dish. Evenly spread barbecue sauce on top of cream cheese mixture. Layer bacon, bell pepper, and tomato on top of barbecue sauce and top with Cheddar cheese. Cover and chill for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: BBQ Bacon Ranch Dip
raw_recipe.description: In this BBQ bacon ranch dip recipe, the flavors of barbecue sauce, cool ranch, and bacon blend together in a perfect dip for your next BBQ event!
raw_recipe.name: BBQ Bacon Ranch Dip

review.reviewBody: This is my recipe, I just wanted to give some tips. When I make this, I mix the cream cheese and ranch packet with a mixer for a couple of minutes. This makes it lighter and not so hard to scoop.

I really thought this combo of ingredients was a little weird, but with the great reviews I decided to give it a shot at my daughter's 3rd birthday party. It was a hit! I read other reviews and saw people had issues with the thickness, so I used about 1/4 c of sour cream since I had it in the fridge in place of some of the cream cheese and then took it out 1 hour before I planned to serve. We had no issues with dipping. I also read others let the cream cheese and ranch sit the night before, so I did do that. I didn't end up using an entire pepper after chopping it in my electric chopper, but everything else was as stated in the recipe. I used sweet baby rays BBQ sauce and Hormel precooked bacon. People were hesitant when I told them the ingredients just Ike I wad, but once they tried it they couldn't stop eating! I served with Tostitos, Fritos, bagel chips, and pita chips. Fritos were definitely the best. It's a keeper;

Okay, here's the deal. I read most of the reviews, as I usually do, and modified the recipe as follows: First, I added three tablespoons of sour cream to the cream cheese/ranch blend. Next, I added a bit more barbecue sauce than the recipe called for. I like barbecue sauce. I mean, I wouldn't drink it or anything, but I do like it, and a bit extra didn't hurt. Third, don't be afraid to add the amount of toppings called for. It might seem like a lot, but trust me, it's not. So be generous with the bacon and veggies. One can never have too much cheese of course. I added some green onions on top for color and a bit more taste. Again, be generous.

Now... this is important... the dip needs a sturdy chip, so I used Fritos. They hold up better than tortilla chips, and you'll appreciate that. Someone suggested putting a knife or spoon out so people could use this as a spread, which would be easier than dipping the Fritos. Either way works... spread would be easier if you don't add the sour cream.

Make this recipe. It's easy. And... bacon. And cheese. I mean, seriously? Why are you still reading this? Get off your butt and make it!

I was really suspicious about this one, but with a couple of edits, this was a HUGE hit. Edits: I used a little more than 1/2 the amount of ranch called for, based on the reviews of others. I also used 1 pack LF cream cheese and 1 pack Neufchatel cheese and whipped it quick with a handmixer -- great consistency. I had some leftover cubed chicken, which I threw in the pan with the BBQ sauce and heated, adding the bacon bits too. I spread the warm mixture over the cheese base and topped with the remaining ingredients. Served with scoops. Perfect game day dish :)

SUPER yum-O! Simply fantastic!!! My hubs and I brought this to our neighborhood cookout this past weekend and it was DEVOURED!!! :) The hostess INSISTED she keep the tiny bit that WAS left for herself lol! This was so good, I was craving it the next day and seriously contemplated making another batch just for myself. I pretty much followed IRISHGINA's directions to the letter except for subbing mild cheddar for the sharp variety (since I was serving a crowd, I wanted to go with a milder cheese). FYI, If you're looking for a decent, affordable sauce, Kraft brand Bulls-Eye (original) was REALLY good in this. NOTES: A mixer works WONDERS to incorporate the Ranch dressing mix with the cream cheese. Of course, you can do this by hand, but I found it MUCH easier using my KitchenAid. Also, it is prefectly fine to sub fat-free or reduced-fat products here (no one will be the wiser). Frito's scoops were perfect dunkers for this sturdy dip. Thanks for sharing your recipe IRISHGINA74! :-)

Even though I tweaked this recipe I am still giving it five stars !! Here is what I did: Added 32 oz sour cream along with the 2 (8 ounce) cream cheese. Used fiesta ranch dip mix instead of plain ranch. Still put in the bacon, tomato and green/red peppers. Left out the b-b-q sauce and shredded cheese. Spiced it up with some garlic powder, onion powder, black and white pepper and season all salt and whipped it all up in my kitchenaid mixer and it was fabulous! I was looking for a dip consistency and the addition of the sour cream was just the right thing. I had tons of requests at work for the recipe. I served this dip with plain chips and tortilla chips and was a huge hit at work. This will be in my general rotation of dips from now on !!

I didn't think this seemingly very simple layered dip would be overly popular at your gathering, but was I ever wrong. Very simple ingredients put together in the right way can be amazing. The only thing I changed was to add 1/4 cup of ranch dressing to the cream cheese layer. I found without it the spread was too firm for my chips.

While I thought this was on the tad salty side, I brought this to a work potluck today and it was GONE! 😮 A hit! And I got lots of compliments so 5 stars for appealing to the crowd! My minor tweaks; added about 1/3 c sour cream when I whipped (using my mixer) the cream cheese and ranch pkt together. I used a red bell pepper vs a green and slipped the tomatoes. To keep it colorful - added some chopped green onions and included them over the red pepper. I let refrigerate all night so my recommend is to let sit out an hour before serving to make scooping and dishing up a bit easier. I did a little head scratching on how this could fit in a pie plate as I had to pivot after my first attempt and ended up putting into a 9x13. Because I plan to make again, I will either use a little less dry ranch OR, see if I can find a lower sodium version. People seemed to enjoy best with Ritz, Club or Wheat Thins. Thanks IRISHGINA74!

I followed the recipe as written except I blended all of the bacon and vegetables together then spread everything over the barbecue sauce. The cream cheese mixture is quite thick and should be thinned out using some sour cream until you get to your desired consistency.

Love this recipe! Every event I make it for, everyone absolutely loves it. I get told to make it every time I attend something. I would recommend mixing the cream cheese & ranch mix 24 hours ahead of time & refrigerating it. It helps make the cream cheese get that ranchy flavor.

I think this was okay. Next time, i would put this in a bigger dish bc the cream cheese was so deap it was hard to get all the flavors together in a pie plate. Next time i will put in a square dish and spread it out thinner, and i think i will actually bake in the oven for 20 min or so on 350 to melt the chedder on the top.

Nothing special about this dip. Also, what seemed like an odd combination of ingredients tasted...well, odd. It was a very pretty dish with the combination of colors provided by the vegetables but that is the only redeeming factor.

This tasted nice, but it’s not really something I would call a dip. Was quite thick and solid after it was put back in the fridge, and I didn’t even keep it in there the whole time. I think it would be better using immediately after it is made at room temperature. I served alongside some crispy chicken fingers and coleslaw for dinner - tasted great with the chicken.

I've made this many times over the years. The key is to use a BBQ sauce you are familiar with and love. I took a shortcut this go around and used real bacon bits. That works good too. This is always a hit and the life of the party!
I wouldn't change a thing. Bacon,ranch,cheddar cheese,cream cheese, tomatoes, bell peppers, and BBQ sauce, what could go wrong?

This was excellent using suggestions from author and others. Used a mixer to mix equal amounts of cream cheese and sour cream (we just prefer a lighter dip.) I let the cream cheese, sour cream and ranch dressing mix sit in fridge for about 8 hours to let the seasonings marry. Also, used a thick BBQ sauce, adding both the sauce and additional toppings about an hour prior to serving. What a hit! Thank you!
I love this recipe and it’s easy in a pinch Bc you have the ingredients oh hand (most of the time). Whenever I serve this people think it’s 7-layer dip and very pleasantly surprised!
Everyone loved it! So easy and delicious.

I was in a hurry so I used 2 tubs of whipped cream cheese. They are 12 oz so I added a little extra Bbq sauce and I also topped the bacon with a can of chicken breast. Super easy and good. An entire green pepper seemed too much so I used 3/4. Next time I’m going to add some hot sauce or jalapeño.
Great!
